newsitem.title: EGYPT: State sale, popular sectors up Cairo bourse volume.
newsitem.headline: State sale, popular sectors up Cairo bourse volume.

text.p: Cements and mills on Tuesday increased turnover on the Cairo bourse which was also buoyed by the government's latest privatisation, the Capital Markets Authority (CMA) report showed.

Despite the most active shares trading lower, the CMA overall index closed 1.24 points up at 364.75 points. Trading was a high 127.66 million pounds ($37.60 million) which included the state's sale of shares worth 21.43 million pounds in Nubareya Agricultural Engineering and Mechanisation.

The CMA report said the state sold 793,750 shares equivalent to 80 percent of the firm. Corporate sources told Reuters each applicant would get about five to six percent only of what they asked for. "This shows that there is a lot of cash waiting for new offers," a corporate source said.
Ihab el-Mahallawi, broker at Intercapital, said the popular milling sector slipped after East Delta Flour Mills said it was cutting its milling prices by 20 pounds a tonne.

He said some investors in the market interpreted the discount as a sign that the milling firms were afraid of competition by the new and more advanced private mills. But the lower share prices attracted new investors, he added.

"(The) discount by one of the millers raised concern in the market about looming competition between the public and private sectors...But the price became very attractive and this resulted in a high volume of trade," he added.
The state has sold some of its stake in the mills but it still maintains the majority. East Delta ended 3.43 pounds down at 67.57.
In the blue-chip cement sector, Helwan Portland Cement shares were the most active and closed at 70.55 pounds, down 1.55, when equity worth 5.6 million pounds were traded.
Egyptian Financial and Industrial, the second most active share, closed 1.00 pound down at 206, when equity worth 4.6 million changed hands.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 517.58 points from 515.84 points and the rarely-traded "closed" firms also rose to 264.89 from 263.98 points.
Out of 95 shares traded, 35 rose and 41 fell while 19 ended unchanged.
